problem:
From **left to right,** the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola $\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{18}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}=1$ are

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $)\,$
and 
$\,($
{{field-3}}, 
{{field-4}} $).$
worked_solution:
To find the $x$-intercepts of the hyperbola, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{18}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{18}-\frac{(0-3)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{18}-1 & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{18} & =2 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =36 \\ x-1 & =\pm 6 \\ x & =1\pm 6 \\ x & =-5,7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are $(-5,0)$ and $(7,0).$
